title: Journeyman report.json
description: The machine-readable result of a `journeyman run`. There is no universal standard for agent process-benchmark reports; this schema IS the contract, versioned with the tool.

schema_version.description: Contract version of this document, bumped only when the schema changes in a way that can break a reader — not on every release. Pin on this rather than on the package version, and stop rather than guess on an unknown value. 1 = the shape published with 0.1.0.

seal.description: The run's identity — change any field and it is a different run.

scene_md5.description: per-scene source hash; pins the exact world

agent_system_md5.description: hash of the submitter's system text, if any

agent_params.description: sampling params sent with every request, verbatim

self_judged.description: true = NOT COMPARABLE; the agent judged itself

nonstandard.description: non-null names the deviation (custom scenes/seeds); also NOT COMPARABLE

axes.description: the profile: one entry per measured axis

score.description: mean over all cells feeding this axis; null when every cell was not-applicable (stimulus never occurred)

n.description: number of cells behind the score (0 when all were not-applicable)

kind.description: how the axis was scored. counted: computed programmatically from replayed events (Scene.event_axes), no judge involved — the score is a fact. judged: a model answered the rubric question and its verdict was matched against the positive label. Anything carrying a score into another system must keep this apart: a counted fact presented as a model's opinion, or the reverse, misstates what was measured.

not_applicable.description: cells excluded because the judge returned na and the axis declares na as not-applicable
